Varlint finds the values in your file that should be variables and are not, tells you which variable each one should be, and binds them.


YOUR IT REVIEW CAN CHECK THIS, NOT TAKE MY WORD

Varlint declares no network access, and Figma prints that on this page beside the last-updated date — so the person who approves plugins where you work can confirm it without contacting me. Your variables and your layers are already in your file; nothing about them leaves your machine, there is nothing to sign in to, and no usage is measured. There is nothing to fill in on a security questionnaire, and no service that can go down and take the plugin with it.


ALL 46 PLACES

Figma allows a variable in forty-six different places: sizes, spacing, corners, stroke weights, fill and stroke colour, every text property, effects, layout grids and component properties. Varlint looks at all of them. That number is not typed in by hand — a test reads Figma's own type definitions and fails if the two ever disagree.


IT SAYS WHICH VARIABLE

Finding a raw value is the easy half. If a variable in your file already holds that value, Varlint names it. If none does, it says so. It never offers to invent variables for you — your token set is yours.


DECISIONS, NOT ROWS

"Every padding of 16 should be spacing/md" is one decision that happens to touch thousands of layers. Varlint shows it as one row with the count on it, so a file's worth of work is a list you can actually read before you agree to it.


IT FOLLOWS YOUR FILE, NOT A RULEBOOK

Varlint reads how far your file has already got in each group — colour, spacing, corners, text — and only ticks the ones you are visibly already doing. A file that has never bound a width is not asked to start. When several variables hold the same value, the one your file already binds there wins. Nothing is guessed from variable names.


WHEN IT CAN'T, IT SAYS SO

Every binding is read back after it is written, and anything that did not take is listed with the reason: the layer is gone, the variable is gone, Figma will not allow it there. A binder that fails quietly is worse than one that fails.


FREE AND PAID

The audit is free, for ever: scan any page or the whole file, see the coverage figures, and see which variable every value should be. $5 once unlocks unlimited binding in every file you open. No subscription.

model.name: Variable Audit
model.description:
Design systems make it easy to answer "where is this variable used?" The harder question is the opposite one: where should a variable have been used, and wasn't? That is the hardcoded #0D99FF on a button, the magic 24px gap, the raw corner radius someone typed in a hurry.


Variable Audit scans your file and answers three questions.



COVERAGE: what is missing

A single adoption score, broken down by category (color, spacing, radius, stroke, typography), by page, and by top-level frame, so you can say "Checkout is at 34%" instead of guessing.


The score separates variables from styles, because a file can score well on color and text styles while using no variables at all. If nothing is bound to a variable, the plugin says so plainly rather than letting styles flatter the number.


Every hardcoded value is listed and ranked by how often it appears, each matched to the variable it should have been. Matches respect variable scopes, so a corner radius token is never suggested for a fill, and every suggestion carries a confidence level. Click any finding to jump straight to the layer.



USAGE: where your variables actually are

A complete map of every binding: which variable, which property, which page, frame and layer. Search it, expand any variable to see its layers, click a row to select that layer on canvas, or select every layer using a variable at once. Run this before renaming or changing a token, so you know what you are about to affect.



CLEANUP: what is actually safe to remove

Local variables that nothing in the file reaches.


Unlike a naive scan, this follows alias chains, so a primitive referenced only by a semantic token is never reported as deletable. Hidden layers are always searched for usage, which means hiding a layer never makes its token look unused.



SCAN WHAT YOU NEED

Scope a run to the whole file, the current page, or just your selection.

Selection and page scans return in seconds, so you can check a frame while you work. A 500,000 layer design system takes a few minutes for a full pass, stays responsive throughout, and any scan can be cancelled part way.



EXPORTS

Everything downloads as CSV: coverage by page and frame, untokenized values with their suggested tokens, per layer detail, the full usage map, and cleanup candidates.



DETAILS

Light, dark and automatic themes, with your choice remembered between runs.


No network access at all. The manifest forbids it, so nothing leaves your machine and nothing is collected. The plugin never writes to your file: suggestions are reported, not applied.



ONE HONEST LIMITATION

Figma gives plugins no way to see whether other files use a variable, so anything published to a library is flagged in the cleanup list. Treat that list as "investigate these", not "delete these".

model.name: Undetach — Tokens & Components
model.description:
Undetach keeps your design system honest, from inside the file — and now it remembers what that system used to look like.


TOKENS

Load your file's variables as an expected set, or define your own typed tokens (color, number, string, boolean). Check drift at a glance — match, drifted, or missing — and push corrections back as real Figma variables with one confirm-gated click.


COMPONENTS

Scan every component with live thumbnails, instance counts as usage bars, and deltas since your last scan. Spot a component trending toward zero before the detach wave hits your library. Find detached-instance candidates and reattach them in one click. Click any row to jump straight to it on canvas.


AUDIT

Find every fill, stroke, corner radius, auto-layout gap, padding, and font size that isn't bound to a variable, each matched to its nearest token. Values that already equal a token simply get bound (no visual change); off-token values snap to the nearest one — and never to a far one, so anything without a close match is left alone. Review findings one by one with the canvas following you (arrow keys to step, Enter to fix), or fix a whole page in one pass. Ignore the exceptions you meant to keep, and they stop coming back.


HISTORY & CHANGELOG

Every push records a named snapshot of your tokens — label, note, timestamp — stored in the file itself, so your teammates see the same history. Compare today's variables against any past snapshot ("this token was

#1D9E75 in v2"), then generate markdown release notes between any two points: tokens changed, added, and removed; components added, removed, and renamed; the biggest usage shifts. One click to copy, ready for your library publish notes, a PR, or Slack.


WHY IT'S DIFFERENT

Figma doesn't record that a frame "used to be an instance," so detach counts from scans are an honest heuristic and labelled as one — a signal to go look, not a verdict. Undetach never guesses at a token that isn't close, never writes without asking, and never sends your file anywhere.


PRIVATE BY DESIGN

No network access, enforced in the manifest. No AI. No data collection. Scans, preferences, and token history stay in your file and in Figma's local plugin storage.


Every write is confirm-gated and undoable as a single step.

model.description:
tokenize finds every raw color and font in a frame, page, or your whole file that isn't yet linked to a color variable or text style, then replaces it with the matching one from your design system — a fast way to audit and clean up design token consistency before a handoff or release.


What it does:

- Scans by frame, page, or entire file, with an option to include hidden layers

- Lists every unlinked color and font, with usage counts, across searchable Colors and Fonts tabs

- Replace with local or library color variables and text styles — or, for fonts, search and apply any font available in Figma directly, even outside the design system

- Locate/Select buttons jump straight to the layers using a given color or font

- Shows exactly how many replacements are mapped before you apply anything

- Dark and light mode, independent of Figma's own theme


One thing to know: for a library style or variable to show up as an option, it needs to already be used somewhere in this file at least once — Figma's plugin API doesn't provide a way to browse an entire library's styles directly, only variables and things already placed in the file. Local styles and variables always show up.


Includes an optional link to support development via Buy Me a Coffee — entirely optional, the plugin works exactly the same either way.
